propositions: Plan-review operations that return a non-degraded PASS verdict do not sign and persist a plan-review attestation by default across all public entry points, leaving the ticket claim-invalid despite incurring full LLM cost.
The library review_plan function defaults sign=True but the CLI and MCP boundaries lack consistent, testable enforcement of the sign-on-PASS invariant at the parser/dispatcher level.
Explicit unsigned execution (--no-sign for CLI, sign=False for library) is not clearly distinguished from default behavior or documented as the exceptional path requiring opt-out.
BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, and local-source results must remain unsigned, and this guard is not pinned at the attest.sign_plan_review artifact boundary where it owns the logic.
Re-invoking a plan review with a current claim-valid attestation must reuse it without re-running the LLM or emitting a duplicate signature, but this idempotent behavior lacks coverage.
PASS verdicts whose signature persistence fails must return a retryable nonzero disposition and identify sign-review as the recovery path, rather than reporting ordinary success.
